case.pattern_description: The undocumented fraud pattern involves structuring multiple online purchases within a brief timeframe, with individual amounts kept just under the $500 authorization threshold to evade detection. It affects cardholders through rapid bursts of unauthorized online activity using compromised card details. The pattern was identified via a Sentinel near-threshold scan analyzing transaction clustering and velocity.

case.summary: Case SEN-011 was opened following a Sentinel sweep on card C00466-K1 belonging to customer C00466, flagging an episode of 4 online transactions totaling $1,860.43 executed within 24 minutes. The transactions were structured just under the $500 threshold with amounts of $463.88, $466.93, $459.07, and $470.55 (transactions 3476601, 3476621, 3476655, 3476664). Graph analysis confirmed a fraud probability of 0.90 based on multiple independent risk signals, including prior confirmed fraud history on the customer. Recommended actions include blocking the card, creating a case, and filing a report under §3a.

sar.narrative: Customer C00466 utilizing card C00466-K1 was subjected to fraudulent activity involving a series of structured online transactions. A total of four transactions (3476601, 3476621, 3476655, 3476664) amounting to $1,860.43 were executed. The activity took place on 2016-11-21 between 20:00:00 and 20:24:00. The transactions occurred via online channels using device profiles including Windows |  | chrome 64.0 |  and |  | chrome 63.0 |. The method involved rapid authorization attempts kept just under the $500 threshold to evade detection. This pattern is suspicious due to velocity, structuring, and the customer's prior confirmed fraud history including cases CC-4662, CC-2680, CC-1708, CC-1400, and CC-1035. No connected cards were identified in this case. Recommended actions include blocking card C00466-K1, creating case SEN-011, and filing a regulatory report.
